What is the main cause of antimicrobial resistance in bacteria?
Antimicrobial resistance arises when bacteria evolve to survive exposure to antimicrobial agents. The primary driver is inappropriate use of antimicrobial agents.
How do bacteria share resistance genes?
Bacteria can transfer resistance genes to other bacteria through conjugation, transformation, and transduction.
What happens when you take antibiotics for a viral infection?
It kills good bacteria and promotes resistance
Antibiotics dont work on viruses but they do kill beneficial bacteria, giving resistant bacteria space to multiply.
Why do antibiotics not work on viruses?
Antibiotics target bacterial structures like cell walls or protein synthesis. Viruses use host cells to replicate and have different structures.
Colds are usually caused by viruses, so antibiotics wont help.
What can happen if antifungal medicines are overused?
Overuse of antifungals selects for resistant fungi like Candida auris, which can cause hard-to-treat infections.
A multidrug-resistant fungus spreading in hospitals
Candida auris is a multidrug-resistant fungus that spreads in healthcare settings and causes serious infections.
Through repeated exposure to antiparasitic drugs
Parasites like malaria develop resistance through mutations when exposed to antiparasitic drugs repeatedly or incompletely.
What is a key strategy to prevent antimalarial resistance?
Complete the full course of treatment
Completing the full prescribed course prevents parasites from surviving and developing resistance.
